source_title: NFL stars Hunter Henry and Justin Jefferson raise $265K for charity as Pat McAfee donates $1M
source_excerpt: NFL players made a powerful impact away from the field in October 2026, turning their influence into meaningful support for people in need. New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry and Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson raised more than $265,000 through charity events, while broadcaster Pat McAfee announced a separate $1 million donation to a children's hospital in Iowa. The three contributions highlighted how athletes and sports personalities can use their platforms to support causes beyond football. From cancer research to the fight against human trafficking and children's healthcare, their efforts put philanthropy firmly in the spotlight.Which NFL players organised charity events in October 2026, and how much did each raise?Hunter Henry and Justin Jefferson led the October fundraising efforts, bringing together supporters for events that connected sports with charitable giving. Their combined total exceeded $265,000, with each player backing a different cause.Henry raised more than $220,000 through his second annual Freedom to Play ping-pong tournament. Jefferson collected more than $45,000 at his inaugural Strike Out Cancer bowling event. Together, their events demonstrated how personal interests and community gatherings can become effective ways to raise money for organisations doing important work.The figures also show how charity events can reach beyond a player's immediate fan base. A tournament or bowling night gives supporters a chance to take part, meet others and contribute to a shared goal. Rather than relying only on direct donations, these events create an experience that encourages people to get involved.McAfee's announcement added another major contribution to the month's charitable activity. The former NFL punter and sports broadcaster pledged $1 million to the University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital following his appearance on ESPN's College GameDay in Iowa City.Unlike Henry and Jefferson, whose totals came from fundraising events, McAfee's contribution was a separate donation. The distinction matters when calculating the overall impact of the announcements. The two NFL players raised more than $265,000 combined, while McAfee announced an additional $1 million pledge for children's healthcare.These efforts offered three different examples of sports-related philanthropy. Henry used a competitive social event to support an international cause, Jefferson organised a bowling event for cancer research, and McAfee directed a substantial gift towards paediatric care.From Boston to Minnesota and Iowa: Where the players' fundraising and donations were directedThe money raised and pledged in October supported three distinct causes, each addressing a different need.Henry's Freedom to Play tournament took place on October 12 at SPIN Boston. The event raised more than $220,000 for International Justice Mission, a global organisation that works to protect people from violence, including human trafficking and other forms of exploitation.The tournament used ping-pong as a way to bring people together around a serious issue. Human trafficking can be difficult to identify and prevent, making public awareness and sustained support important parts of the wider response. Funds raised through events like Henry's can help support organisations working with vulnerable communities.For Henry, the event also offered a way to connect his professional life with a cause beyond the New England Patriots. The success of the second annual tournament showed that a charity event can build momentum when organisers return with a clear purpose and invite supporters to take part.Jefferson's fundraising took a different approach. The Minnesota Vikings star held his first Strike Out Cancer bowling event, raising more than $45,000 for the American Cancer Society.Cancer affects patients, families and communities in ways that extend well beyond treatment. Research, patient support and public education all require resources. Jefferson's event helped direct money towards an organisation involved in the fight against the disease, while giving participants a social setting in which to support the cause.The inaugural event also established a starting point for future fundraising. Although one event cannot address every need associated with cancer, it can attract attention to the cause and encourage people to continue supporting research and patient services.McAfee's donation was directed towards the University of Iowa Health Care Stead Family Children's Hospital. His $1 million pledge followed his appearance on College GameDay, which visited Iowa City.The hospital provides specialised care for children, making charitable support particularly important for patients and families facing complex medical needs. Donations can help hospitals strengthen their services, support patient programmes and improve the care environment. The precise allocation of McAfee's pledge should be confirmed with the hospital before attributing it to a particular programme or treatment.The three contributions therefore addressed different challenges, from protecting vulnerable people to supporting cancer-related work and children's healthcare. Their destinations also reflected the reach of sports philanthropy across local communities and wider charitable networks.How NFL stars are using their platforms to support communitiesProfessional athletes have a level of public visibility that can help charitable causes attract attention. However, the impact of that visibility depends on what follows the headlines. Fundraising events turn interest into participation, while donations provide direct financial support to organisations.Henry's ping-pong tournament and Jefferson's bowling event offered supporters an accessible way to contribute. Both activities created opportunities for people to gather around a cause without requiring them to be football experts or even regular NFL viewers.That approach can be valuable because successful fundraising often depends on more than a single large gift. Community events can bring in donations from many participants, introduce new supporters to an organisation and encourage repeat involvement. They can also give charities opportunities to reach audiences they might not otherwise engage.McAfee's pledge demonstrated another route to impact. A large donation can provide an organisation with substantial financial support, although the ultimate effect depends on how the funds are allocated and the needs they are intended to meet.The three announcements also show why charitable work deserves attention alongside on-field performances. NFL stars are often judged by touchdowns, tackles, records and results. Their community efforts offer a different measure of influence, one based on the causes they support and the people who may benefit.Still, the fundraising totals alone do not reveal the full long-term impact. The number of people helped, the programmes funded and the results achieved will depend on the recipient organisations' work. Those details are important when assessing the lasting value of any charitable contribution.What the October 2026 charity announcements mean for the NFL communityThe October initiatives provided a reminder that the NFL's influence extends well beyond stadiums and television broadcasts. Henry and Jefferson raised more than $265,000 combined, while McAfee announced a separate $1 million donation to a children's hospital in Iowa.Their efforts also highlighted the variety of ways public figures can support charitable work. One event brought attention to human trafficking, another supported cancer research, and a major hospital pledge focused attention on children's healthcare.For the Patriots and Vikings communities, Henry and Jefferson's events offered a chance to connect their support for football with causes that affect people's lives. For Iowa, McAfee's announcement placed children's healthcare at the centre of a major charitable pledge.The next measure of success will be how effectively the money reaches the intended causes and supports their work. Fundraising totals make headlines, but the lasting value lies in what organisations can do with the resources they receive.For now, the three announcements stand as notable examples of sports figures directing their influence towards charitable goals. Their October efforts showed that the impact of football personalities can extend far beyond the field, reaching people and organisations working to meet urgent needs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
